stops.note: Franz Anton Mesmer developed his theory of 'animal magnetism', a supposed invisible fluid he claimed to channel into patients, in Vienna in the 1770s
Mesmer's Paris séances became a craze until a royal commission including Benjamin Franklin and Antoine Lavoisier concluded in 1784 that the effects came from imagination
first 'to hypnotise', then 'to fascinate', as mesmerism gave way to James Braid's 'hypnotism' in the 1840s

current_meaning: to hold someone's attention completely; to hypnotise
